title: Intel Unveils Robotics AI Platform Uniting Real-Time Control, AI on One Chip
key_facts: Intel unveiled its Robotics AI Suite and Physical AI Studio at an invitation-only workshop in Seoul on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026.
It pitches the Core Ultra Series 3 processor (CPU, GPU and NPU on one die, up to 180 TOPS) as a single-chip alternative for real-time control, AI inference and sensor processing.
John Healy, vice president and general manager of Intel's Industrial and Robotics Division, said "Our first competitive advantage is openness."
Physical AI Studio supports Nvidia's GR00T N1 among training targets.
Intel-commissioned survey of 800 leaders: about 60% expect robot fleets within five years, 40% have a formal strategy.
Tech Times says the question will be answered by production deployments, and Nvidia Isaac has a multi-year head start.
quote_evidence: Intel unveiled its Robotics AI Suite and Physical AI Studio at an invitation-only workshop in Seoul on Wednesday, staking out a position as a full-stack platform provider for factory and logistics automation
These figures are Intel-commissioned and should be read as market positioning, not independent research.
why_it_matters_hint: Intel is trying to make factory robots cheaper to build by running control and AI on one chip.
notes: Company launch; claims not independently validated.
